sections.heading: Why we are writing to you

sentences.text: We are writing because CHD2-related epileptic encephalopathy and SCN1A-related seizure disorders are placed on the same mechanism road: too little protein from loss of function of one copy.
The phenotype similarity score between the two conditions is high at 0.2722.
Shared features listed in the pack include atonic seizure, generalized myoclonic seizure, tonic seizure, febrile seizure between 3 months and 6 years, and seizure precipitated by febrile infection.
The gene-disease link is marked definitive for both CHD2 and SCN1A in Gene2Phenotype.
Both communities also have a patient organization listed in the pack.

For CHD2, the pack lists Coalition to Cure CHD2 and a CHD2 Natural History Project, and it also says CHD2 is included in Simons Searchlight, the RARE-X Data Collection Program, and the Citizen Health natural history program.
For SCN1A, the pack lists two natural history or registry studies, NCT06504511 and NCT06967727, and says SCN1A is also included in Simons Searchlight.
The transfer review says registry design and natural history protocol are transferable between the two conditions.
The transfer review also says outcome measures and endpoints are transferable, with review of age of onset and severity before any tool is adopted.
The transfer review says clinical networks, sites, and investigators are also transferable.

sections.heading: What we would like to learn from or reuse

sentences.text: We would like to learn from or reuse SCN1A registry and natural history data items, consent, and visit schedules where they fit CHD2.
We would like to review SCN1A outcome measures and endpoints as possible templates for CHD2 studies.
We would like to learn which clinics, sites, and investigators already care for families with a similar seizure picture.
We would also value expert advice on whether SCN1A trial design could serve as a template for CHD2, because the pack marks this as needing expert review rather than ready transfer.

The pack says SCN1A has targeted clinical trials at the gene level, including 7 trials with highest phase 3, while no targeted clinical trial was found for CHD2 in the searched ClinicalTrials.gov source.
The pack says no approved disease-specific therapy was found for CHD2.

For SCN1A, the pack lists cannabidiol, fenfluramine, and stiripentol as approved disease-specific therapies for Dravet syndrome, but it also marks them as symptom treatments or says mechanism is not established.
We must not assume the two conditions share the same variant direction in every patient.
The reason is that published SCN1A cases include variants acting in more than one direction, including contested gain claims, so which mechanism applies depends on the individual variant.
We also must not assume an SCN1A animal or cell model can stand in for CHD2, because the pack says the neighbor's model is gene-specific.
The pack also says mechanism is recorded per gene and disease, not per family, so a family's own CHD2 variant should be confirmed by a clinical geneticist before acting on transfer ideas.
The pack says the curated mechanisms for CHD2 and SCN1A are inferred from variant types rather than functional studies.
The SCN1A organization listing also passed only an automated check, and the pack says no human has verified it.
The pack does not assert enrolment in an SCN1A trial for a CHD2 family.
One SCN1A trial in the pack, NCT06872125, specifically excludes gain-of-function variants.
Which direction for SCN1A do you consider established, and on what evidence, given the published disagreement noted in the pack.
Is Dravet Syndrome Foundation the right contact for SCN1A-related seizure disorders, and does it run a registry.
Has our child's specific CHD2 variant been functionally classified as loss of function, gain of function, or dominant negative, and does it match the mechanism recorded for the condition.
What functional evidence exists for CHD2, given that the curated mechanism is inferred from variant types rather than functional studies.
Thank you for reading.

glossary.meaning: A change that reduces how much a gene works or how much working protein is made.
The features and symptoms seen in a person or group.
A study that follows people over time to learn how a condition changes.
A result a study measures to judge change, such as seizure counts or daily function.
A change in a gene's DNA sequence.
A doctor who interprets gene findings in the context of the person and family.
